title: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025
sponsor_context: Formal sponsor of H.R. 5009, the originating legislative vehicle; the NDAA text was substituted later in the process.
last_action: Enacted as the Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025.
summary: The FY2025 NDAA strengthened protection of advanced AI from adversary access, launched defense AI-and-biotechnology work, improved human-factors and evaluation infrastructure for military AI, and established the NSA Artificial Intelligence Security Center.

substance_sections.title: Advanced-AI national-security duties
substance_sections.summary: Directs the CDAO Governing Council to identify AI models that could create national-security risks, develop strategies to prevent adversary access, and recommend legislative or administrative action.

substance_sections.title: AI and biotechnology pilot program
substance_sections.summary: Creates a pilot program to develop and demonstrate near-term AI and machine-learning applications for biotechnology and national-security missions.

substance_sections.title: Analysis of prohibition on broadcast and distribution of digitally manipulated intimate images under the Uniform Code of Military Justice
substance_sections.summary: Directs the Defense Department to assess whether to clarify the military offense of indecent viewing, recording, or broadcasting to cover digitally manipulated intimate images. The FY2026 NDAA explicitly expands the analysis to nonconsensual deepfakes and sets a reporting deadline.

substance_sections.title: Prohibition on procurement of covered semiconductor products and services from companies providing covered semiconductor products and services to Huawei
substance_sections.summary: Bars the Defense Department from entering into or renewing covered semiconductor procurement contracts with entities knowingly providing covered semiconductor products or services to Huawei. Requires a vendor certification process and allows limited national-security waivers.

substance_sections.title: Reports on approval and deployment of lethal autonomous weapon systems
substance_sections.summary: Requires annual Defense Department reports to congressional defense committees on lethal autonomous weapon systems approved, waived, under review, or not approved under Directive 3000.09. FY2026 NDAA § 1061 expands the review information to include specified legal reviews.

substance_sections.title: Establishment of Department of Defense working group on multilateral artificial intelligence coordination
substance_sections.summary: Creates a Defense Department working group with allies and partners for joint AI testing and interoperability, multilevel security of training and operational data, and control of jointly generated technical data under participating countries’ export laws.

substance_sections.title: AI Human Factors Integration Initiative
substance_sections.summary: Establishes an initiative to study and improve how people interact with military AI, including operator trust, workload, decision-making, testing, and design guidance.

substance_sections.title: Advanced computing infrastructure for AI
substance_sections.summary: Directs the Defense Department to plan computing infrastructure that supports the development, testing, evaluation, and deployment of advanced AI capabilities.

substance_sections.title: Budgeting for AI data
substance_sections.summary: Requires Defense Department AI programs to estimate and budget for the data needed to train, maintain, and improve models, including data preparation, labeling, protection, and sustainment costs.

substance_sections.title: AI-enabled weapon-systems center of excellence
substance_sections.summary: Requires an evaluation of a center of excellence to share lessons, safety guidance, standards, benchmarks, training, and partner experience for AI-enabled weapon systems.

substance_sections.title: NSA Artificial Intelligence Security Center
substance_sections.summary: Establishes an AI Security Center within NSA's Cybersecurity Collaboration Center to develop counter-AI guidance and promote secure AI adoption for national-security systems and the defense industrial base.

committee_dynamics: These provisions were enacted through the annual defense and intelligence authorization vehicle rather than as standalone AI statutes. H.R. 5009 originally addressed wildlife-trafficking sanctions; the FY2025 NDAA text was later substituted into that vehicle, so David Joyce is the formal originating-bill sponsor rather than the NDAA's principal author.
advance_rationale: Enacted law; implementation replaces advancement forecasting.

responsible_agencies: Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council
Joint Service Committee on Military Justice

deadlines.requirement: Establish the Artificial Intelligence Security Center within the NSA Cybersecurity Collaboration Center within 90 days of enactment.
Establish or designate the multilateral AI working group.
Procurement prohibition begins and the Defense Department must implement a vendor certification process.
First annual report due to congressional defense committees.
Submit the analyses under § 569F as amended by FY2026 NDAA § 563.
Working group terminates unless extended on national-security grounds.

agency_status.detail: The enacted duties and organizational requirements are verified; a comprehensive official implementation assessment has not yet been completed for this grouped record.

title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024
sponsor_context: Sponsor of H.R. 2670, the bill that became the FY2024 NDAA.
last_action: Enacted as the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024.
summary: The FY2024 NDAA created or expanded military and intelligence-community safeguards for AI acquisition, vulnerability testing, generative-AI detection, responsible use, and oversight of AI-assisted intelligence analysis.

substance_sections.title: Congressional notification of changes to Department of Defense policy on autonomy in weapon systems
substance_sections.summary: Requires the Secretary of Defense to brief congressional defense committees within 30 days of modifying Directive 3000.09 on autonomy in weapon systems and explain the changes.

substance_sections.title: Review and plan relating to cyber red teams of Department of Defense
substance_sections.summary: Requires a Defense Department cyber red-team capability plan that accounts for foreign threats using AI or machine learning, updated red-team standards, implementation guidance, and annual progress reporting.

substance_sections.title: Control and management of Department of Defense data; establishment of Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council
substance_sections.summary: Establishes the CDAO Governing Council for responsible use of AI and data. Requires guidance on ethical safeguards, bias mitigation, and access or distribution restrictions for AI models and evaluation resources.

substance_sections.title: Management of data assets by Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer
substance_sections.summary: Directs the CDAO to apply AI analytics to defense cyber data assets, coordinate with the Defense Department’s privacy and civil liberties official to ensure lawful data handling, and provide semiannual congressional briefings.

substance_sections.title: Course of education and pilot program on authentication of digital content provenance for certain Department of Defense media content
substance_sections.summary: Requires a Defense Media Activity course on digital forgeries and a pilot to authenticate the provenance of official Defense Department images and video. The statutory definition of digital forgery expressly includes AI and machine learning.

substance_sections.title: CDAO acquisition authority
substance_sections.summary: Extends the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer's special acquisition authority through fiscal year 2029 and requires plans and demonstrations showing how it will deliver operational AI capabilities.

substance_sections.title: AI bug-bounty programs
substance_sections.summary: Directs the Defense Department to develop a bug-bounty program for foundation models being integrated into military missions and operations.

substance_sections.title: Generative-AI detection and watermarking competition
substance_sections.summary: Creates a prize competition to evaluate and transition tools that detect generative-AI content and apply or identify watermarks.

substance_sections.title: Responsible-AI plans and security strategy
substance_sections.summary: Requires responsible-AI guidance and accountability metrics, a strategy addressing generative-AI cybersecurity and adversarial uses, and plans to secure Defense Department models, data, and algorithms.

substance_sections.title: Study of vulnerabilities in military AI
substance_sections.summary: Requires a study of military-AI privacy, security, accuracy, explainability, testing, auditing, traceability, emergent behavior, and supporting test infrastructure.

substance_sections.title: Establishment of the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of State
substance_sections.summary: Creates a State Department chief AI officer with duties to evaluate and oversee responsible departmental adoption and advise the Secretary on ethical AI use in diplomacy.

substance_sections.title: Programs for next-generation microelectronics in support of artificial intelligence
substance_sections.summary: Directs the Director of National Intelligence, subject to funding, to establish or oversee a microelectronics research program whose required research focus includes safety and controls for generative AI applications in the intelligence community.

substance_sections.title: Rules for AI-assisted intelligence products
substance_sections.summary: Requires the Director of National Intelligence to assess and update analytic and sourcing rules so intelligence products appropriately disclose and support the use of AI and machine-learning tools.

substance_sections.title: Intelligence-community AI policies
substance_sections.summary: Requires common policies for acquiring, using, testing, documenting, monitoring, and securing intelligence-community AI capabilities, including third-party models and data.

committee_dynamics: These provisions became law through the annual defense-authorization vehicle rather than as standalone AI statutes. H.R. 2670 was introduced as the FY2024 NDAA by House Armed Services Committee Chair Mike Rogers.

title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026
sponsor_context: Formal sponsor of S. 1071, the originating legislative vehicle; the NDAA text was substituted later in the process.
last_action: Enacted as the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026.
summary: The FY2026 NDAA established new defense and intelligence safeguards for national-security AI research, biological data, model and supply-chain security, testing and oversight, frontier-AI planning, and intelligence-community use of public models.

substance_sections.title: National Security and Defense AI Institute
substance_sections.summary: Establishes a collaborative institute to support national-security and defense AI research, education, workforce development, testing, and transition into operational use.

substance_sections.title: Biological data for AI
substance_sections.summary: Directs the Defense Department to improve the security, availability, and responsible use of biological data for AI while addressing biotechnology, adversary-access, and national-security risks.

substance_sections.title: Analysis of potential modifications to the offense of wrongful broadcast or distribution of intimate visual images under the Uniform Code of Military Justice
substance_sections.summary: Requires the Defense Department to assess whether and how to clarify the military offense of wrongful distribution of intimate images to cover nonconsensual deepfakes, and report the results to Congress.

substance_sections.title: Notification of waivers under Department of Defense Directive 3000.09
substance_sections.summary: Requires written congressional notification within 30 days of issuing a waiver under the Defense Department’s autonomy-in-weapons directive. Adds legal-review information to the FY2025 NDAA’s autonomous weapons reporting requirement.

substance_sections.title: Defense-wide AI and machine-learning security
substance_sections.summary: Requires a department-wide cybersecurity and governance policy covering AI-specific attacks, supply-chain risk, life-cycle security, testing, auditing, monitoring, training, and incident response.

substance_sections.title: Security requirements for AI procurement
substance_sections.summary: Requires risk-based physical, cyber, workforce, supply-chain, monitoring, and incident-reporting standards for AI systems procured by the Defense Department.

substance_sections.title: Collaborative cybersecurity education
substance_sections.summary: Creates Defense Department partnerships with academic institutions to strengthen cybersecurity curricula, competencies, workforce pathways, and federal coordination; it supports the workforce needed to secure AI systems but is not itself AI-specific.

substance_sections.title: AI considerations in cybersecurity training
substance_sections.summary: Requires mandatory Defense Department cybersecurity training to cover the distinctive cybersecurity challenges created by AI use.

substance_sections.title: Guidance and prohibition on use of certain artificial intelligence
substance_sections.summary: Requires removal of covered DeepSeek- or High Flyer-linked AI from Defense Department systems and restricts contractor use in performing Defense contracts, subject to waivers. Also directs the department to consider guidance on other covered AI companies posing national-security risks.

substance_sections.title: AI model assessment and oversight
substance_sections.summary: Creates a cross-functional team to establish a standardized framework and governance structure for evaluating and enabling Defense Department AI models.

substance_sections.title: AI sandbox environments
substance_sections.summary: Creates a task force to build secure environments for AI experimentation, training, familiarization, model evaluation, and responsible deployment across the Defense Department.

substance_sections.title: AI Futures Steering Committee
substance_sections.summary: Establishes a senior Defense Department committee to plan for advanced and frontier AI capabilities, examine risks and governance, and address safeguards including meaningful human control and override.

substance_sections.title: Appropriate scoping of artificial intelligence research within the National Nuclear Security Administration
substance_sections.summary: Limits use of NNSA appropriations for AI research, applications, and infrastructure to the agency’s nuclear-security missions. Preserves specified reimbursable support that does not interfere with those missions.

substance_sections.title: NSA AI security guidance
substance_sections.summary: Directs the NSA Artificial Intelligence Security Center to issue guidance protecting advanced AI and its supply chain from nation-state theft, sabotage, and compromise.

substance_sections.title: Intelligence-community AI development and use
substance_sections.summary: Strengthens intelligence-community AI leadership, coordination, reuse, acquisition terms, and tracking of model performance, safety, fairness, transparency, accountability, and trustworthiness.

substance_sections.title: Public AI models in classified environments
substance_sections.summary: Applies intelligence-community AI policies to public models hosted in classified systems and requires risk-based testing, benchmarks, and secure evaluation environments.

substance_sections.title: DeepSeek prohibition
substance_sections.summary: Bars DeepSeek from intelligence-community systems, subject to limited exceptions and required security mitigations.

committee_dynamics: These provisions were enacted across the defense and intelligence divisions of the FY2026 NDAA. S. 1071 originally addressed postal-service matters; the NDAA text was later substituted into that vehicle, so John Cornyn is the formal originating-bill sponsor rather than the NDAA's principal author.
advance_rationale: Enacted law; implementation replaces advancement forecasting.

responsible_agencies: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
Joint Service Committee on Military Justice
